title: FSSAI Issues Notices to Nestlé, HUL Over Misleading Horlicks, Resource Claims
excerpt: The regulator flagged Horlicks bone-health and birth-weight claims, Nestlé's unapproved Resource Renal powder and inconsistent Nescafé labels — and sanctioned prosecution against Priyagold's maker, Dodla Dairy and Ueir Organic Foods in the same sweep.
body:
• FSSAI has issued show-cause notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) over misleading claims and labelling lapses, with further action possible if their replies are unsatisfactory.
  • At HUL, the notices cover Horlicks Women's Plus (bone-health, "healthy muscles" and "No Added Sugar" claims) and Horlicks Mother's Plus ("Healthy Birth Weight" claims).
  • At Nestlé India, FSSAI flagged Resource Renal powder for lacking mandatory prior approval and a veg/non-veg mark, and three Nescafé ready-to-drink products for inconsistent category declarations.
  • Reader check: treat the flagged bone-strength, birth-weight and "no added sugar" claims as unproven for now — check the back-of-pack nutrition table and ingredient list (Women's Plus contains maltodextrin) rather than front-of-pack promises.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Saturday that it has issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever over misleading claims and non-compliances on several products, following recent inspections and audits. The notices are part of a wider sweep in which prosecution has also been sanctioned against three smaller food companies.

What FSSAI flagged at Hindustan Unilever

FSSAI issued two notices to HUL, both concerning Horlicks. On Horlicks Women's Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink 400g, it said claims including "Nutrition for Strong Bones", "Clinically Proven to Help Improve Bone Strength in 6 Months" and "Improves Bone Health" were misleading or non-compliant. It objected to "healthy muscles", saying the wording contravened rules governing use of the term "healthy", and called the "No Added Sugar" claim misleading because the product contains maltodextrin. The claim of "100 per cent RDA of Calcium, Vitamin D & K2" also did not comply, and nutritional information was not provided in the prescribed form, according to The Hindu BusinessLine and Mint.

On Horlicks Mother's Plus Kesar 400g, FSSAI said "Healthy Birth Weight" and "For baby's healthy birth weight" were potentially misleading.

What FSSAI flagged at Nestlé India

Nestlé India faces two findings. Resource Renal Vanilla Flavour Powder, described as food for the dietary management of individuals with conservatively treated chronic kidney disease, requires prior FSSAI approval under the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, and Prebiotic and Probiotic Food) Regulations, 2022 — approval FSSAI said was not obtained. The label also lacked the mandatory vegetarian or non-vegetarian mark.

Three Nescafé ready-to-drink products — Intense Café Cappuccino, Choco Mocha and Chilled Latte — declared "Flavoured Milk" on the front and "Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink" on the back, while e-commerce listings called them "Coffee Flavoured Milk". FSSAI said they fall under "Flavoured Milks", making the proprietary-food declaration incorrect.

The rule behind the notices

The mechanism is the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, read with the Labelling and Display Regulations, 2020. A health claim is not ordinary marketing copy: claims must be truthful and scientifically substantiated, claims that a food can prevent, treat or cure a disease or physiological condition are prohibited unless specifically permitted, and wordings such as "healthy" and "no added sugar" may be used only when prescribed conditions are met. A special-medical-purpose product may also need prior approval. FSSAI's case is that each flagged product fails one or more of those tests.

How the companies have responded

HUL said its two Horlicks products comply with all applicable requirements and that it will share "scientific and regulatory evidence" with the authorities, in an emailed response reported by Mint. Nestlé India did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Sunday, according to the same reporting. Both companies must reply within the stipulated period, and FSSAI has warned of further action if a response is unsatisfactory.

A wider crackdown

In parallel, FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Surya Food & Agro, maker of Priyagold biscuits, after an inspection found bran meant for cattle feed used as a fibre source; its licence had already been suspended. Prosecution was also sanctioned against Dodla Dairy, after a referral laboratory confirmed a full-cream milk sample was unsafe due to detergent/caustic soda and substandard on milk fat, and against Ueir Organic Foods over pesticide residues in yellow raisins, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The licences of Sukhdarshan Pharma and Bala Ji Food Products were also suspended. "The authority maintains zero tolerance for any food safety violations or compromises on public health as per FSS Act 2006," the regulator said.

What happens next

Each company must now explain the flagged claims and labelling, after which FSSAI decides whether the matter closes, labels and listings must be corrected, or further action follows under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Until then, shoppers should read the back of the pack — nutrition table, ingredient list and category declaration — on Horlicks Women's Plus, Mother's Plus, Resource Renal and the Nescafé ready-to-drink range, rather than the health promises on the front.
